message.content: {"label":"sufficient","reason":"All essential facts about Uber's revenue sources are explicitly supported by the retrieved passages: Ridesharing, Uber Eats, Other Bets (Freight, New Mobility), and Other revenue (Vehicle Solutions), plus revenue recognition context.","supported_requirements":[{"requirement":"Ridesharing revenue is generated from the ridesharing platform (booking fees and related revenues) and is linked to Ridesharing Gross Bookings.","passage_rank":3,"quote":"This increase was attributable to an increase in Ridesharing Gross Bookings of $8.8 billion, or 26%, compared to 2017. Ridesharing revenue as a percentage of Ridesharing Gross Bookings increased from 21% in 2017 to 22% in 2018. This increase was primarily due to higher booking fees, offset by a $0.3 billion increase in Driver incentives."},{"requirement":"Uber Eats revenue is generated from the Uber Eats platform and is tied to Uber Eats Gross Bookings (with service fees contributing to revenue).","passage_rank":3,"quote":"Uber Eats revenue for 2018 increased by $0.9 billion, or 149%, to $1.5 billion compared to $0.6 billion in 2017. This increase was attributable to an increase in Uber Eats Gross Bookings of 164% compared to 2017."},{"requirement":"Other Bets revenue includes Uber Freight (pre-determined per-shipment fee) and New Mobility.","passage_rank":1,"quote":"• Uber Freight. Other Bets primarily consists of Uber Freight, which we publicly launched in 2017. We generate revenue from our Uber Freight offerings from shippers that pay us a pre-determined fee for each shipment to use our brokerage service.\n\n• New Mobility. We introduced New Mobility in 2018. Revenue is generated through fees charged to consumers for a ride on a dockless e-bike or e-scooter."},{"requirement":"Other revenue includes Vehicle Solutions (wind-down noted).","passage_rank":3,"quote":"Other revenue for 2018 decreased by $135 million, or 35%, to $255 million compared to $390 million in 2017.
